L’honneur voulait qu’on résistât jusqu’à la dernière extrémité.

glosses: To believe; to put credence in.

examples.text: Someone said there were over 100,000 people there, but I can't credit that.

glosses: To add to an account.

examples.text: Credit accounts receivable with the amount of the invoice.
For the payroll period credit employees' tips to their wages paid account and debit their minimum wage payable account.
The full amount of the purchase has been credited to your account.

glosses: To acknowledge the contribution of.

examples.text: I credit the town council with restoring the shopping district.
Credit the point guard with another assist.

glosses: To bring honour or repute upon; to do credit to; to raise the estimation of.

examples.text: You credit the church as much by your government as you did the school formerly by your wit.

glosses: Reliance on the truth of something said or done; faith; trust.

examples.text: When Jonathan and the people heard these words they gave no credit into them, nor received them.

glosses: Recognition, respect and admiration.

examples.text: I give you credit for owning up to your mistake.

 Of credit and renown,

glosses: Acknowledgement of a contribution, especially in the performing arts.

examples.text: She received a singing credit in last year's operetta.

glosses: Written titles and other information about the TV program or movie shown at the beginning and/or end of the TV program or movie.

examples.text: They kissed, and then the credits rolled.

examples.text: In view of your payment record, we are happy to extend further credit to you.

glosses: The time given for payment for something sold on trust.

examples.text: a long credit or a short credit

examples.text: What do you mean my credit is no good?

glosses: An addition to certain accounts; the side of an account on which payments received are entered.

examples.text: Didn't you know that the IRS will refund any excess payroll taxes that you paid if you use the 45(B) general business credit?

glosses: A source of value, distinction or honour.

examples.text: That engineer is a credit to the team.

examples.text: To repair your star cruiser will cost 100,000 credits.

glosses: A nominal unit of value assigned outside of a currency system.

examples.text: Would you like to play? I put in a dollar and I've got two credits left.

Le respect de la personne humaine, la fidélité sexuelle et le dévouement pour les faibles constituent les éléments de moralité dont sont fiers tous les hommes d’un cœur élevé —c’est même très souvent à cela que l’on réduit la morale.
Puis il fallut écouter les compliments des paysans et leurs doléances enveloppées dans des protestations de respect.
Le général Sarrail commande la place de Verdun. Le 44ᵉ régiment de R.A.T. occupe la ville. Le général exige une discipline stricte, prescrit les marques extérieure de respect.

glosses: Souci de ne pas porter atteinte à cette personne ou à cette chose.

examples.text: Je savais bien que ces protestations ne servaient à rien et que, dans ces circonstances, en appeler au respect de la légalité devant ces brutes était ridicule.

L’équipe du journal Charlie-Hebdo, qui marquera beaucoup plus que Berthes ou Foucault la culture française, pratique au contraire joyeusement la désintégration syntaxique de la langue. Mais il est frappant de constater que leur manque de respect pour les règles de l’école communale n’entame pas la clarté du texte. Au contraire, l’équipe du Collège de France respecte formellement la langue pour mieux détruire le sens.

glosses: Soumission; obéissance.

examples.text: Respect du code de la route, des conventions sociales

glosses: Hommage ; civilité.

examples.text: Je vous devais mes respects et quelques avances de bonne amitié ; veuillez les accepter comme je vous les offre, de tout mon cœur.

Quand j'allai lui présenter mes respects, je trouvai la porte ouverte et dépourvue du factionnaire de rigueur, et pour cause ; l'armée permanente de l'Islande se réduit à deux policemen, dont les gourdins suffisent à maintenir l'ordre le plus parfait sur toute l'étendue du territoire.
Avant de quitter Bruxelles, j'étais allée rendre mes respects aux Breughels du Musée d'Art Ancien.

Un jour il se présente au Colonel avant un départ en mission : « Mon Colonel, je venais vous prier déféremment d’accepter mes respects ». L'adverbe était si bien dans la note professionnelle que tous les assistants, dont le Colonel, ont éclaté de rire, sans que le type comprenne leur hilarité.

glosses: Sert à exprimer, de manière concise, son respect, sa considération ou son admiration.

examples.text: Il a tout fait tout seul ! Franchement, respect !

glosses: To recite numbers in sequence.

examples.text: Can you count to a hundred?
The psychiatrist asked her to count down from a hundred by sevens.

glosses: To determine the number of (objects in a group).

examples.text: Count the number of apples in the bag and write down the number on the spreadsheet.

The President of the Senate shall, in the presence of the Senate and House of Representatives, open all the certificates and the votes shall then be counted;
The person having the greatest number of votes for President, shall be the President,[…]
How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.

glosses: To amount to, to number in total.

examples.text:
They counted thirty, crowded in a space
Which left scarce room for motion or exertion; […]

glosses: To be of significance; to matter.

examples.text: Your views don’t count here.
It does count if you cheat with someone when you’re drunk.

glosses: To be an example of something: often followed by as and an indefinite noun.

examples.text: Apples count as a type of fruit.
This excellent man […] counted among the best and wisest of English statesmen.

Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too.[…]But as a foundation for analysis it is highly subjective: it rests on difficult decisions about what counts as a territory, what counts as output and how to value it. Indeed, economists are still tweaking it.

glosses: To consider something as an example of something or as having some quality; to account, to regard as.

examples.text: He counts himself a hero after saving the cat from the river.
I count you as more than a friend.

The entertainment we haue had of him,
Is far from villanie or ſeruitude,
And might in noble mindes be counted princely.

glosses: To reckon in, to include in consideration.

examples.text: They walked for three days, not counting the time spent resting.

glosses: To take account or note (of), to care (for).

examples.text: […]to make her faire, that no man counts of her beauty.

glosses: To recount, to tell.
To plead orally; to argue a matter in court; to recite a count.
The act of counting or tallying a quantity.

examples.text: Give the chairs a quick count to check if we have enough.

glosses: The result of a tally that reveals the number of items in a set; a quantity counted.

examples.text: By the official count, there are something like thirteen hundred species of birds in the Amazon, but Cohn-Haft thinks there are actually a good many more, because people have relied too much on features like size and plumage and not paid enough attention to sound.

glosses: A countdown.

examples.text: Zou, who was living in Elephant and Castle, south-east London, was convicted of 11 counts of rape, with two of the offences relating to one victim. glosses: The number of balls and strikes, respectively, on a batter's in-progress plate appearance.

examples.text: He has a 3–2 count with the bases loaded.

glosses: An object of interest or account; value; estimation.

examples.text: When he was readie to his steede to mount / Vnto his way, which now was all his care and count.
